title: SERAC external memory values with Mirror code compression
hypothesis: With SERAC retrieval keys and scope classifier held fixed, shared counterfactual value basis plus one Mirror angle per edit will retain on-scope target behavior and off-scope deferral while reducing actual memory payload bytes versus explicit values; retrieval errors must be measured separately from value reconstruction.
physical_object: shared 16D counterfactual value plane and SERAC key memory
mirror_coordinate: one per-edit value angle and shared value basis
controls: SERAC explicit per-edit key and value vectors with exact shared scope classifier
generic Cartesian value coefficients over the same shared plane
Mirror angle-coded values with identical key retrieval

task.query: exact key, 4 paraphrases key+Gaussian noise sigma 0.03, and 256 unrelated random queries
task.retrieval: nearest cosine key with fixed threshold 0.90; identical for all methods
task.value: fixed-norm counterfactual vector on a known 2D plane
metrics: unrelated false-trigger rate and output drift
value decode MAC and measured lookup latency

development.allowed: fixed value orbit and 0.90 scope threshold; no fresh-dependent changes

paid_objects: explicit output values or shared value basis

success_gate: Every fresh world at N64: exact and paraphrase hit recall >=99%, unrelated false-trigger rate <=1%, on-scope NRMSE <=1e-5, actual Mirror payload <=80% SERAC; compare actual bytes and quality with generic Cartesian shared-plane code.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses retrieval, value-quality or N64 storage gates; if generic coefficients match or beat Mirror bytes at equal quality, no Mirror-specific advantage is claimed.
boundaries: Synthetic external-memory mechanism screen, not a SERAC model reproduction.
Scope retrieval is intentionally identical and oracle-simple for every method; retrieval and value-code effects are reported separately.
Counterfactual values are hand-aligned to a fixed-norm 2D orbit; no natural edit generation or learned basis discovery.
deviations: Lookup timing repetition count increased after initial timing showed an outlier; fresh metrics were rerun under the same frozen worlds/seeds and no configuration changed.
